treatments.name: Vocabulary and sentence clarification
treatments.description: Reduces lexical and syntactic load: unnecessary jargon, over-long sentences, indirect phrasing and unresolved references. Content and order untouched.
treatments.boundary_note: Must not reorder concepts, add examples or analogies, add headings, or add mechanism detail. Sentence-level only.

treatments.name: Prerequisite-aware concept sequencing
treatments.description: Reorders the explanation so no idea arrives before the ideas it depends on, using the concept dependency analysis. Wording left alone.
treatments.boundary_note: Must not simplify vocabulary, add examples, or add formatting. Reordering and minimal connective tissue only. This is what makes H2 testable.

treatments.name: Mechanism and causal explanation
treatments.description: Turns description into mechanism: what happens, why, how the parts interact, and the intermediate steps the source skipped.
treatments.boundary_note: Must not simplify vocabulary, reorder the overall structure, or add analogies. Adds causal detail in place.

treatments.name: Concrete examples and analogies
treatments.description: Adds one worked example and, if useful, one analogy — each explicitly mapped to the concept, with the limits of the mapping stated.
treatments.boundary_note: Must not simplify vocabulary, reorder concepts, or add formatting. Adds grounding only, and only where the plan says it is warranted.

treatments.name: Structural and visual presentation
treatments.description: Applies structure that reveals the conceptual shape: headings, short paragraphs, ordered steps for procedures, a table where a comparison is genuinely being made, and a diagram specification where flow matters.
treatments.boundary_note: Must not change wording, order, or content. Pure presentation — this is what makes H3 (presentation vs comprehension) testable.

treatments.name: Audience adaptation
treatments.description: Re-pitches the explanation for a specific learner profile by changing what is assumed and what is unpacked — not by changing the facts.
treatments.boundary_note: Must not change technical content. Adjusts assumed prior knowledge and depth of unpacking only. Expect the expertise-reversal effect: more scaffolding should help beginners and hinder advanced learners.

prompt_conditions.name: Condition A — Default (no pedagogical instruction)
prompt_conditions.description: No system prompt. Captures default model behaviour. Intentionally empty: any instruction here would itself be an intervention.

prompt_conditions.name: Condition B — Generic tutor prompt
prompt_conditions.description: The conventional one-line tutor instruction. Represents ordinary prompting practice so Condition C is tested against a fair baseline.

prompt_conditions.name: Condition C — Structured pedagogical prompt
prompt_conditions.description: Specifies a teaching process rather than a writing style, with explicit anti-patronising and anti-padding constraints.

dimensions.question: Can each individual statement be understood on first reading?

anchors.1: Most sentences require re-reading; dense or convoluted throughout.
anchors.3: Generally followable; several sentences carry too many ideas at once.
anchors.5: Each sentence lands on first reading without loss of precision.

dimensions.question: Does each part follow from what came before?

anchors.1: Ideas appear in an order that does not build; jumps are frequent.
anchors.3: Mostly ordered, with some ideas arriving before their groundwork.
anchors.5: Every step rests on something already established.

dimensions.question: Are concepts the reader needs first actually provided first?

anchors.1: Relies throughout on knowledge it never supplies.
anchors.3: Supplies some prerequisites; assumes others silently.
anchors.5: Needed prerequisites are introduced before use, without padding.

dimensions.question: Does it explain how and why, not only what?

anchors.1: Definitions and assertions only; no causal account.
anchors.3: Some mechanism, with intermediate steps left implicit.
anchors.5: Causes, interactions and intermediate steps are explicit.

dimensions.question: If examples or analogies are used, do they aid understanding?

anchors.1: Examples are decorative, unrelated, or actively misleading.
anchors.3: Relevant examples, but the mapping to the concept is left implicit.
anchors.5: Example is apt, mapped explicitly, and its limits are stated. Score 5 also applies if no example was needed and none was given.

dimensions.question: Is it pitched at the stated learner, neither over nor under their head?

anchors.1: Badly mismatched: unexplained expert content, or patronising basics.
anchors.3: Roughly right with stretches that miss the level.
anchors.5: Consistently pitched at the stated learner.

dimensions.question: Is complexity intrinsic to the subject rather than added by the writing? (5 = no added complexity)

anchors.1: Heavy added complexity: avoidable jargon, indirection, padding.
anchors.5: All remaining difficulty belongs to the subject itself.

dimensions.question: Is substantive content preserved rather than dropped? (5 = nothing lost)

anchors.1: Essential content, caveats or qualifications are missing.
anchors.5: Content is intact; any simplification is of expression, not substance.

dimensions.question: Is it internally consistent and free of claims it cannot support? (5 = no problems detected)

anchors.1: Contains claims that contradict each other or are plainly unsupported.
anchors.3: Mostly sound with one or two questionable assertions.
anchors.5: No problems detected. This is not verification of correctness.
